facts.value: Equines are social animals and usually live in groups or herds.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines communicate with each other through a range of vocalizations, body language, and scent cues.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines engage in playful behavior, particularly when they are young.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines are known for their strong flight response, meaning they are quick to flee when they perceive a threat.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines establish a social hierarchy within their herd, where each member has a specific rank and role.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: This hierarchy is established through aggressive displays and physical interactions such as biting, kicking, and pushing.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines are strictly herbivorous and spend a considerable amount of their day grazing on grass or other vegetation.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: They have evolved specialized teeth and digestive systems to efficiently break down and extract nutrients from tough plant matter.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines can sleep standing up, which is a unique adaptation that allows them to rest and stay alert at the same time.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: They can also lay down to sleep, but usually only do so for short periods.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines are polygamous animals, meaning they can have multiple mates throughout their lives.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines are viviparous animals, meaning they give birth to live young that develop inside the mother's womb.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Generally, equines give birth to a single offspring per gestation, although there have been rare cases of twins or even triplets.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Although equines can have multiple heats a year, they generally breed every two years.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines display a remarkable ability to adapt to various environmental conditions.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick
